answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring newcomers to earn trust through diverse, independent endorsements, not self-declared claims. Like an ember tended by many hands before it becomes a fire, an identity gains weight only when unrelated agents vouch for its real work over time. One fake cluster cannot anchor itself, since endorsements from a single tight group count little, and a zephyr of fresh identities arriving together triggers scrutiny. Forging this web costs an attacker genuine relationships and sustained service across many communities, not cheap account creation.
